skill.name: python-executor
skill.description: Run Python scripts through the inference.sh Python executor with common data, web, media, and document libraries available.
skill.summary: Run short Python jobs through a remote sandbox with popular Python libraries preinstalled.
skill.author: inference-sh-skills

security_audit.summary: Most static shell findings are Markdown backticks or examples, but the skill intentionally routes code through the external belt CLI and inference.sh. Confirmed risks include remote arbitrary Python execution, outbound network examples, mutable install dependencies, and automatic returned output files; no prompt injection text was found.

remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval before each belt run, show the exact code and target service, and warn users not to send secrets.
Pin CLI and related skill installation sources, document trusted versions, and avoid directing users to mutable raw installation scripts.
Ask users to approve target domains before web scraping or API calls, and document that remote code can make outbound requests.
Limit returned files to intentional outputs and warn users not to write private data into outputs.

content.user_title: Run Python Tasks in a Remote Sandbox
content.value_statement: Many AI workflows need short Python jobs without local setup. This skill runs Python through inference.sh with common analysis, scraping, media, and document libraries.
actual_capabilities: Runs Python snippets with configurable timeout through belt.
Uses preinstalled libraries for data, scraping, browser automation, images, video, documents, and 3D files.
Returns files saved under outputs, including charts, CSVs, images, videos, PDFs, and 3D models.
Supports data analysis, visualization, web scraping, API calls, media processing, and document generation.
Offers default and high-memory variants for larger workloads.
limitations: Requires the inference.sh belt CLI and login before use.
Runs CPU-only jobs and does not provide GPU acceleration.
Code execution is non-interactive, so scripts must save outputs instead of opening windows.
User code may access networks if written to do so; review code before execution.

use_cases.title: Analyze data tables
use_cases.description: Process CSV or pasted data, calculate summaries, and return charts or transformed files.

use_cases.title: Automate approved web tasks
use_cases.description: Fetch approved pages or APIs, extract structured information, and save results as files.

use_cases.title: Generate media and documents
use_cases.description: Create images, videos, PDFs, and 3D assets from short Python scripts.

prompt_templates.title: Run a small calculation
prompt_templates.prompt: Use python-executor to run a short Python script that summarizes this data: [paste data]. Return the printed result and any output files.

prompt_templates.title: Create a chart
prompt_templates.prompt: Use python-executor to build a chart from this table: [table]. Save the chart to outputs/chart.png and summarize the result.

prompt_templates.title: Scrape an approved page
prompt_templates.prompt: Use python-executor to fetch [approved URL], extract [fields], and save a CSV in outputs. Use a timeout of [seconds].

prompt_templates.title: Build a processing pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Use python-executor to process [input files], call [approved API], generate [report type], and return all files saved in outputs.

output_examples.input: Analyze a two-column sales table and create a bar chart.
output_examples.output: Printed summary with total sales, average sale, and top seller. Returned chart image saved as chart.png.

output_examples.input: Resize a batch of product images and export compressed copies.
output_examples.output: Returned resized image files and a short log listing dimensions and filenames.

output_examples.input: Fetch an approved API endpoint and make a CSV report.
output_examples.output: Returned CSV file plus a concise summary of records fetched and fields extracted.

best_practices: Review generated Python before execution, especially network requests and file output paths.
Keep secrets out of prompts and code sent to remote execution.
Set practical timeouts and save intentional artifacts under outputs.
anti_patterns: Running unreviewed code from unknown sources.
Sending private data, API keys, or credentials to the executor.
Using the skill for long-running, interactive, GPU, or production workloads.

faq.question: Does this run Python locally?
faq.answer: No. It sends jobs through the inference.sh belt CLI to a remote sandboxed executor.

faq.question: What libraries are available?
faq.answer: The skill lists common libraries for data, HTTP, scraping, browser automation, images, video, PDFs, and 3D processing.

faq.question: Can it access the internet?
faq.answer: Yes, submitted Python can use HTTP libraries when the code makes network requests. Approve target domains before running it.

faq.question: How are generated files returned?
faq.answer: Files saved under outputs are detected and returned with the execution response.

faq.question: Should I send secrets to this skill?
faq.answer: No. Do not include API keys, credentials, private data, or regulated data in remote execution jobs.

faq.question: Does it support interactive plots?
faq.answer: No. Scripts should save plots and other artifacts to files instead of opening interactive windows.
